title: Simultaneous Spectrum-Imaging Acquisition in High-Energy Electron Energy-loss Spectrometry and X-ray Energy Dispersive Spectrometry
content: Various types of signals can be generated in a scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) and can be effectively utilized for imaging and analysis of a thin specimen. For example, signals caused by inelastic scattering of the incident electrons with the specimen, such as energy-loss electrons and characteristic X-ray, offer elemental/chemical information at a beam position. Therefore, it is essential to simultaneously collect those signals related to specimen chemistry via electron energy-loss spectrometry (EELS) and X-ray energy dispersive spectrometry (XEDS) together with images for development of advanced materials and devices. We have developed a higher energy EELS system based on a CEOS energy-filtering and imaging device (CEFID) [1], which expands from a conventional energy range (∼3,000 eV) to 13,000 eV or higher in collaboration with JEOL/JEOL USA and CEOS. And The system was installed to an existing aberration-corrected S/TEM JEOL JEM-ARM200CF at Lehigh together with a new scanning generator called MDP. In order to acquire high-energy EELS signals, not only the CEFID system but also STEM instrument itself have been optimized. The high-energy EELS system can be controlled by CEOS Panta Rhei and JEOL FEMTUS platforms. In fact, through the newly developed JEOL FEMTUS data acquisition/analysis platform, simultaneous XEDS and high-energy EELS spectrum-imaging (SI) datasets can be obtained. In this study, we summarize the instrument optimization procedures for higher energy EELS signal detection first, and then simultaneous high-energy EELS and XEDS SI acquisition is described.
